newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-TRACY ENDS DROUGHT WITH NAZARETH INDY CAR TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-TRACY ENDS DROUGHT WITH NAZARETH INDY CAR TRIUMPH.

text.p: Canada's Paul Tracy went from the penalty box to the winner's circle on Sunday with a triumph at the Nazareth 225-mile (362-km) CART Indy Car race in a Penske Mercedes-Benz.
Tracy, penalised $25,000 two weeks ago for rough driving at Long Beach, California, ended a personal 27-race winless streak and Team Penske's 20-race winless streak in the process.
"This is one of the greatest races of my life," said Tracy after taking the checkered flag in race that ended under caution.
Tracy averaged 118.919 mph (191.4 kph) finishing 0.527 of a second ahead of local favourite Michael Andretti, in a Swift Ford, followed by Al Unser, Jr. in another Penske Mercedes-Benz.
Tracy, the pole sitter, led three times for 186 laps total around the one-mile oval.
Andretti took the lead from Tracy on lap 35 only to pit on lap 53 due to a flat tyre, dropping him to 17th place.
Tracy led the last 141 laps but the Canadian was pressured at the end.
Lap by lap Andretti sliced his way through traffic and with less than 50 laps remaining he was in second place.
As numerous cautions slowed the race Andretti caught up to Tracy but could not pass for the lead. "The only thing was missing, was I ran out of time," said Andretti.
With three laps remaining a slower car caught fire bringing out the 10th caution of the day.
Andretti leads the points standings with 51 followed by American Scott Pruett at 47 and Tracy at 45.
The next race in the 17-race series will take place in Rio de Janeiro on May 11.
